entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Saint Sava, known as the Enlightener or the Illuminator, was a Serbian prince and Orthodox monk who became the first Archbishop of the autocephalous Serbian Church. Born in the 12th century, he was exiled to Mount Athos, Greece, where he received spiritual guidance from the monk St. Athanasius. In 1219, he returned to Serbia and was elected as the Archbishop, uniting the Serbian Orthodox Church under a single leadership. He played a crucial role in the unification of the Serbian people, fostering a sense of national identity and promoting the use of the Serbian language and alphabet. Saint Sava also founded the University of St. Sava, one of the oldest universities in the Balkans, and wrote several theological works, including the treatise 'The Law of the Serbian People'. He died on January 21, 1236, and was later canonized as a saint by the Serbian Orthodox Church. His legacy continues to shape Serbian identity and culture to this day.
